search_log.why: Core sources use purposive/theoretical sampling but vary in their treatment of saturation and do not fully reflect recent critiques.
search_log.concept: information power; saturation; reflexive thematic analysis sample size
search_log.selection: Peer-reviewed methodological articles directly addressing sample adequacy and method-specific saturation.
search_log.changed: Replaced any universal saturation rule with methodology-specific adequacy and added information power as a planning heuristic.

search_log.why: Core sources include coding, themes and reliability but a platform must prevent hybridization of incompatible TA families.
search_log.concept: reflexive thematic analysis; codebook TA; coding-reliability TA; intercoder reliability
search_log.selection: Braun and Clarke's current methodological papers, a worked RTA example and a peer-reviewed ICR methods article.
search_log.changed: Separated reflexive TA from codebook/coding-reliability TA and made ICR method-gated rather than universal.

search_log.why: Business core sources sometimes treat participants as information providers, whereas sociological sources raise co-production.
search_log.concept: active interview; interview interaction; focus group interaction; feminist focus groups
search_log.selection: Seminal monograph and peer-reviewed methodological critiques/primers.
search_log.changed: Interview and focus-group records now require an explicit account of interaction, group process and the status of participant accounts.

search_log.why: Core ethnography is strong but rapidly changing digital, multi-sited and patchwork forms require current qualification.
search_log.concept: multi-sited ethnography; patchwork ethnography; digital ethnography; contextual privacy; internet research ethics
search_log.selection: Seminal review, current peer-reviewed development, academic monographs and recognized AoIR guidance.
search_log.changed: Qualified uninterrupted immersion and added platform visibility, contextual privacy and online/offline field boundaries.

search_log.why: Core materials contain interpretive, business and cross-case traditions that make different generalization claims.
search_log.concept: case study generalization; theory building from cases; intrinsic instrumental case study
search_log.selection: Seminal peer-reviewed methodological articles and major academic monographs representing competing traditions.
search_log.changed: Added explicit case-study tradition and generalization fields; preserved Stake/Yin/Eisenhardt disagreement.

search_log.why: Generic grounded-theory labels conceal incompatible procedures and epistemologies.
search_log.concept: Glaserian; Straussian; constructivist grounded theory; situational analysis
search_log.selection: Foundational and current specialist methodology monographs.
search_log.changed: Required variant-specific coding, theoretical sampling and saturation/sufficiency; treated situational analysis as distinct.

search_log.why: Core sources offer coding and matrices but require clearer modern method-specific workflows.
search_log.concept: qualitative content analysis approaches; framework method; matrix analysis
search_log.selection: Widely used peer-reviewed methods articles and specialist academic monograph.
search_log.changed: Separated content-analysis variants, clarified units and counts, and added the framework matrix workflow.

search_log.topic: Narrative, conversation, discourse and phenomenological distinctions
search_log.why: Core introductory coverage risks generic code-and-theme processing across specialist traditions.
search_log.concept: narrative inquiry; small stories; conversation analysis sequence; discourse under-analysis; descriptive phenomenology; IPA
search_log.selection: Seminal monographs and peer-reviewed methodological articles for each tradition.
search_log.changed: Added unit-specific analysis and prohibited generic thematic substitution for sequence, story form or phenomenological reflection.

search_log.why: Core handbooks preserve multiple genres but evaluation standards are contested.
search_log.concept: analytic versus evocative autoethnography; photo elicitation; photovoice; arts-based research
search_log.selection: Seminal debate articles and academic method texts.
search_log.changed: Created genre-specific quality rules and separated visual/participatory claims from automatic empowerment.

search_log.why: Core handbooks support co-production and decolonization but platform rules need sharper power and sovereignty safeguards.
search_log.concept: participatory research power; participation tyranny; Indigenous methodologies; decolonization not metaphor; intersectionality methodology
search_log.selection: Seminal peer-reviewed articles and recognized academic monographs authored within the relevant traditions.
search_log.changed: Defined participation by decision rights, added community data sovereignty and rejected a universal decolonization badge.

search_log.why: Core materials endorse combinations but could be read as convergence-only or method pragmatism without integration.
search_log.concept: mixed methods integration; triangulation; joint displays; meta-inference
search_log.selection: Seminal organization article, peer-reviewed integration framework and reporting standards.
search_log.changed: Made integration mandatory for mixed-method claims and retained discordance as a possible finding.

search_log.why: Most core books predate operational generative AI, while the platform needs current, evidence-based governance.
search_log.concept: ChatGPT qualitative data analysis; query-based analysis; AI thematic analysis; epistemological incongruence; AI reporting transparency
search_log.selection: Peer-reviewed methodological experiments and frameworks published in 2023-2026; excluded blogs and vendor claims as authority.
search_log.changed: Classified AI evidence as emerging/contested; required human final authority, source verification, disclosure, privacy governance and method-specific feature gating.
